data.narrative: Wrote a blameless postmortem covering the service's incident classes, critiqued a deliberately bad postmortem and cataloged every anti-pattern, then rewrote it and upgraded the original with the blind spots revealed.

dimension_scores.observation: Every contributing factor names a system or a missing gate, never a person; the rewrite eliminated all six 'John' references and converted them to pipeline gaps.
dimension_scores.evidence: postmortem-linkops.md CF1-CF10 all system-subject; postmortem-rewritten.md CF1-CF5 all system gaps; blame-check sections present.

dimension_scores.observation: Traced the migration bug to a systemic root cause and proved local testing could not have caught it (bug only manifests at production scale), locating the cause in the missing staging gate.
dimension_scores.evidence: postmortem-rewritten.md: 'the deployment pipeline did not require migrations to pass against a staging database with production-like data'.

dimension_scores.observation: Rewritten timeline uses exact UTC timestamps with measurements (migration applied 14:02, p95 40ms->9.8s at 14:05, rollback 14:17, recovery 14:19) and derives the 16-minute affected window.
dimension_scores.evidence: Both postmortems contain precise UTC event tables, not 'Friday afternoon'.

dimension_scores.observation: All remediations are owned, deadlined, and stated as checkable outcomes (CI blocks merge, GitHub blocks without 2 approvals, release tool rejects Friday deploys).
dimension_scores.evidence: R1-R10 in postmortem-linkops.md with Owner, Deadline, Checkable outcome columns; R1-R5 in postmortem-rewritten.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Used the bad postmortem as a mirror: identified that the original lacked deadlines and measured impact, and fixed both rather than defending the draft.
dimension_scores.evidence: postmortem-linkops.md gained deadlines on R1-R10 and a measured Impact section after the critique.

dimension_scores.observation: Both documents answer 'what happened AND what we change' with structural remediations and a single prioritized lesson; not incident reports in postmortem clothing.
dimension_scores.evidence: One-lesson section ('enforce cross-layer contracts structurally') plus owner-backed remediation tables in both artifacts.

strengths: Applied the S3 standard automatically: every remediation changes the system, not the person.
The 'would local testing have caught it?' test correctly relocated the root cause from the operator to the pipeline.
Self-critique via the fictional postmortem produced concrete, verifiable improvements to the original draft.
growth_areas: Could add a monitoring/drill section describing how each remediation will be verified under a simulated recurrence.
The fork's readiness-gap finding (ready does not check the worker) is identified but not yet remediated as code.
data.recommendation: Implement R8 (ready probes worker liveness) in the fork as the structural follow-up, and run a blameless postmortem drill with a simulated recurrence.

public_evidence.student_action: Wrote a broad-scope postmortem for the service incidents, then critiqued a bad postmortem and rewrote it from blame to systems language, upgrading the original with deadlines and measured impact.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Two artifacts: postmortem-linkops.md (R1-R10 with Owner/Deadline/Checkable) and postmortem-rewritten.md (systemic root cause, system-gap CFs, precise UTC timeline).
public_evidence.proof: Timeline derived a 16-minute affected window; impact quantified at ~2,300 users; no person named in any factor.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows a candidate who treats postmortems as organizational debugging: systemic root cause, structural remediations, and self-critique.
